test_title: PYST 8: SSC CPO - English Comprehension (Held On 12 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Choose the correct direct sentence of the following sentence.

He said that the lights had gone off during the storm.

options.text: He said, "The lights go off during the storm."
He said, "The lights had gone off during the storm."
He said, "The lights went off during the storm."
He said, "The lights have gone off during the storm."

solution:
The correct answer is '**He said, "The lights went off during the storm."**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To convert **Indirect Speech** into **Direct Speech**, the tense is generally changed back to its original form.
 
• The reporting clause **"He said"** remains unchanged.
 
• The Past Perfect Tense (**had gone off**) in indirect speech changes back to the **Simple Past Tense** (**went off**) in direct speech.
 
• Thus, the correct direct speech is: *"He said, **'The lights went off during the storm.'**"*
 
• **Option 1** is incorrect because *"go off"* is in the Simple Present Tense.
 
• **Option 2** is incorrect because the Past Perfect Tense is retained instead of being changed back.
 
• **Option 4** is incorrect because *"have gone off"* is in the Present Perfect Tense.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

**Correct Direct Speech:** *"He said, **'The lights went off during the storm.'**__"*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• When converting **Indirect Speech** to **Direct Speech**, restore the original tense wherever appropriate: 

 
 
• Past Perfect → Simple Past
 
• Past Continuous → Present Continuous
 
• Past Simple → Present Simple (depending on context)
 
 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• Indirect: *She said that she had finished her work.*
 
• Direct: *She said, "I finished my work."*
